heading: The eleventh day of October, in the seventh year of Kunrad IV. Third desk, second floor. Four matters heard.
_day_seconds_note:
MEASURED, NOT GUESSED. tests/play_day.tscn at dwell 8 -- a competent reading pace -- spends 337 s across these four matters. At the authored 1200 s that is burn 0.28: Tuesday was oversupplied three and a half times over, the candle never left its fresh state, the light contracted by four per cent, and GUTTERING_FROM was unreachable on any day the player finished. Three separate authored systems -- the melting stub, the contracting reach, the gutter -- had never once been rendered in ordinary play.

520 puts that same player at burn 0.65, so the last matter of the day is worked by a candle past the guttering line, and it makes the skill the books already teach worth something: the Kalendar's own head says it keeps Thurn's dead and nobody else's, the Matrices plate says a Marchfeld die is almost never dead, so a notary who has read them can tell from the charter alone which books can possibly speak about this packet. Skipping the three that cannot is a 45 s matter against an 85 s one. At 1200 s that skill bought nothing whatever.

A slow player (dwell 16, 592 s) loses the fourth matter, which is a lesson and not a wall: Thursday's slots carry it forward through requires_ruled/fallback, and Saturday holds it after that.

Do not raise this without re-running tools/sweep_pacing.ps1 across the whole dwell range. One point on that curve is how you get a retune that is exactly wrong for everybody except the imaginary player you measured.
burnt_out_text: The candle went before the queue did. The doorkeeper turned the rest of them out into the passage and told them to come back on Thursday.

case_slots._note: The knife. Placed last on Tuesday deliberately: the player has just been handed a case where two laws disagree and told that referring is the only honest answer, and then one more man comes in with a packet where every check they have been taught comes back clean. It is the day's sting in the tail and it sets up Thursday.

opening_documents._note: THE DIE, AT THE MOMENT OF TEMPTATION. Case 01's whole visible surface is a seal rubbed to nothing and its correct verdict is CONFIRM; the trap is 'damaged therefore false', and the game's opening move is to punish the reflex the player walked in with. On the memorandum this sat in a paragraph with nine other instructions. Keyed to the glass going onto wax, and again to reaching for the Book of Matrices, because those are the same thought. Same document id in both entries: _deliver_investigation_arrivals dedupes on doc.id for the whole session, so it arrives exactly once.

document.title: Memorandum
document.claim_summary: A live die can leave a bad mark; a dead die cannot leave any mark at all.

opening_documents._note: The second key for the same leaf.

document.title: Memorandum
document.claim_summary: A live die can leave a bad mark; a dead die cannot leave any mark at all.

opening_documents._note: THE TABLET'S SECOND VERB, once there is something worth writing down. Scratching is discovered in three seconds by moving the nib; erasing is not, and this is the only statement of it anywhere. Delivered in the gap after the first matter, where _burn_the_day is not running and the reading is free.

document.title: Memorandum
document.claim_summary: Scratch down what you cannot hold in your head, and rest the nib on the wax to take it out again. Nobody will ever read it but you.

opening_documents._note: THE FLAME, AS A DIAGNOSIS RATHER THAN A VERB. The practice leaf teaches the gesture and the player performs it before the first knock; what this adds is when to reach for it unprompted. Keyed to the act, so on cases 01-03 — which carry no erasure findings — it arrives as the answer to 'I tried that and nothing happened'. Deliberately NOT keyed to after_case case_03: delivering 'hold up a parchment you cannot fault' in the gap immediately before the knife would telegraph the day's authored sting.

document.title: Memorandum
document.claim_summary: When a parchment is wrong and you cannot say where, pick it up and put it in front of the flame. Skin that has been scraped is thin, and thin skin lets the light through.

opening_documents._note: THE THREE RINGS, in the gap before the matter they decide. Case 03 is the contested reckoning and the first time CONFIRM and DENY are a choice of law rather than a finding of fact. Case 02 ends in a hard clean DENY on a dead die, so this reads as the syllabus moving on rather than as a hint about the next packet. The Almanac says the same at greater length on pages 4 and 5, but that is spread 2 of 3 and two page-turns in.

document.title: Memorandum
document.claim_summary: When two laws disagree, CONFIRM or DENY names the law you chose. REFER follows this office's procedure without choosing. Do not confuse procedure with truth.

_leaf_placement_note:
THE FOUR MEMORANDUM LEAVES LIE ON THE MEMORANDUM, and the positions are measured rather than chosen. They were first placed by eye and every one of them landed under something: the rings leaf under the candle, where line four read 'confuse procedure with truth.' as a complete inverted sentence; the tablet leaf under the magnifying glass, hiding 'the nib on the wax', which is the game's only statement of the erase verb; the die leaf across the top half of the docket, covering the petitioner's name at the moment you judge his wax; and the flame leaf across the pendant seal on the one case that is about that seal.

bring_to_front CANNOT save a leaf from the candle (z_index 1) or the glass (z_index 2). Higher z draws above all lower-z siblings whatever child order says, so the only fix is to land somewhere else. Measured obstacles: candle x 704..800 y -189..-41, lens home x 545..785 y -125..355, docket x -500..-190 y -254..64, seal x -245..-141 y 171..334, charter x -254..164 y -356..466.

On the memorandum is also where they BELONG: they are further leaves of the same document, in the same hand, and the doorkeeper is working through a pile that was left beneath the Register. They cover only the sentences already read and fixtures the player can move, never evidence.
